summary: A card from Guatemala and the page it opens. The address printed on the card never changes; the page behind it keeps growing, in Spanish first with English under it.
license_note: MIT is the parent repo's grant and covers this page and the project code. The card artwork is the owner's: commissioned by them, excluded from the MIT grant by NOTICE at the repo root, served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt. Nothing in this manifest enlarges what NOTICE withholds — to reuse the artwork, ask the owner.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own. /gt/ is a page inside mrdirno/vibe-cards, published on that repo's Pages surface, and its MIT is inherited from the parent repo rather than chosen here. The card came before the page: its four faces were commissioned from Meta AI by the card's owner and arrived finished. NOTICE at the repo root keeps all four out of the MIT grant, so listing this page makes nothing about the artwork reusable. Fragment Mono and Instrument Serif are embedded under SIL OFL 1.1 (OFL.txt).
origin_audit: The long version, kept because the short one is what a reader gets and this is what it was cut from. Not a fork and not a repository of its own: /gt/ is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards (GitHub reports fork=false), the seed repo of this registry, published on that repo's Pages surface. Its MIT is INHERITED from the parent repo's LICENSE, not chosen for it, and it covers the page and the code only. The card came before the page: the four faces were commissioned from Meta AI by the card's owner and arrived finished — src/web/app.js says at the head of the GT-001 template block 'Finished artwork, placed and not rebuilt', 'a card someone has already designed', 'the original was approved' — and NOTICE at the repo root excludes all four from the MIT grant, so being listed makes nothing about the artwork reusable. The faces entered the tree 2026-08-13T04:20:30Z (first commit touching src/web/templates/gt-archive-back.jpg, commits API, anonymous), three days after the repo was created and a few hours AFTER this registry file's first commit at its current path — so on disk the registry is slightly older than this page, while the card's design predates both, and its paper-and-approval history is the owner's, not this file's to reconstruct. Fragment Mono and Instrument Serif are embedded in the page under SIL OFL 1.1 (OFL.txt, repo root and site). The living entries in src/site/gt/entries.json are the project's own on the only authorship record that exists for them (NOTICE's closing section). GT-001 sat in this registry's held list until 2026-08-16, and the standard's own v1.0.1 amendment used /gt/ as the page that met the account-free wish rule while the seed's own landing page failed it.
_note: L0, not L1. The three L0 clauses hold: this file is served at the url the card's chip carries, the page it names takes a wish without an account, and LICENSE at the repo root is real SPDX MIT. Not L1 yet, because L1 wants terminal states recorded in public and this project's queue is not published.
_wish_channel_was_a_mailto: Until 2026-08-17 this field published the owner's personal email address at a permanent public url, and argued for it at length: the page's own route was a mailto, so the field declared what was real. The page's mailto was removed that morning after the card's holder asked twice from a phone — 'remove the email thing on the Guatemala card saying it will reach a real person' — and the page now posts into the same wishing well every other card page uses. This file was not changed with it, so the address kept being served here for another eight hours, in a file the network gate fetches on every run. Two lessons, and the second is the one that generalises. FIRST: a card's page and a card's manifest are two public surfaces, and fixing one is not fixing the card. SECOND: an address printed on a chip can never be recalled, so a personal address must never be the declared route on any surface a chip opens — not because email is a bad channel, but because this one cannot be taken back. tools/verify_pages_artifact.mjs check 7b now refuses a mailto: wish_channel in every manifest this repository publishes or carries, so this cannot return by being re-argued. Stated precisely, because the first draft of this sentence said 'refuses a mailto: wish_channel outright' and an independent pass read that as covering the whole file and found it false: the NETWORK arm still accepts a mailto from a third-party project's manifest, deliberately, because an account-free inbox is a real channel and the standard says so. What 7b refuses is our own surfaces, where the url is on a chip.
